prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Alder Creek Electrical Distribution Substation supplies transformer/feeder bays/distribution circuits within approved limits. Bay Automation Controller (Juniper) produces Bay Status Digest for Station Supervisory Control System (Glasswing); timestamps changes/presents status. North Bay Controller/South Bay Controller have non-substitutable scopes; boundaries define device authority/confirming indications; shared equipment requires coordination. North blocks closing on unready interlocks. Approved sequences specify order/holds/stops. Breaker Control Unit executes authorized commands subject to modes/authority/selection/interlocks/availability/procedures; local authority prevails. North Protection Panel protects north-side scope; Transformer Protection Panel retains independent authority. Feeder Protection Relay (Tandem) independently protects/trips with approved settings; produces Relay Diagnostic Note. Glasswing produces Alarm Acknowledgement Slip; separates current/archival evidence; local indications prevail. Station Gateway carries authorized communications, produces Protocol Retry Summary; verify currency after outages. Maintenance Remote Terminal cannot override local authority. Satellite Time Receiver (Bluefin) supplies time/Clock Drift Snapshot to Sequence Event Archive (Orchard) for correlation; reference-loss requires holdover/quality marking, not deletion; timing validates neither measurements nor protection. Station DC System powers protection/automation; produces retained Battery Load Test Record. Orchard preserves sources/times/quality/order/uncertainty/corrections/configuration/access-history; role-restricted/audited; retention/holds require authorized release; test ingestion/capacity/recovery/readability; protect backups. Engineering Workstation restricts revision-controlled configurations/history; produces Settings Review Receipt; approved bounded searches/exports preserve timestamps/quality, label derived ordering, separate conclusions. Protection Relay Engineer (Larkspur) reviews coordination/events/diagnostics; revisions require studies/independent approval/work-window/comparison/testing; discrepancies block release. Substation Supervisor oversees procedures/availability, resolves priorities/confirms exceptional authority. Switching Desk Coordinator (Keystone) maintains cross-bay plan, checks clearances/work, produces Isolation Boundary Card, confirms handback; evidence remains engineering-reviewable. Control Room Operator requests equipment/change/timing; coordinates access/suspension/resumption; reviews sequences/alarms: priority/source/time/bay, new/standing/corroboration, protection/condition/service significance; protection operations/unexplained states require prompt investigation. Substation Field Crew (Cinder) verifies authorization/hazards/boundaries/device identity/local conditions/isolation/absence-of-energy—not screens; logs presence/maintains communications; stops/escalates

New part:
S151: The Control Room Operator acknowledges alarms only after reviewing the indication and retains awareness of any condition that remains unresolved.
S152: The Control Room Operator uses the acknowledgement slip to record the alarm response and any outstanding action.
S153: The operator checks available device status and sequence information without treating a cleared indication as proof that the underlying cause has been corrected.
S154: The Feeder Protection Relay indication is reviewed against the affected feeder status and any related protection operation.
S155: The Bay Automation Controller provides bay-level status indications that support the operator’s assessment of the alarm.
S156: Glasswing shall retain alarm state and event information for operator review after an indication has cleared.
S157: The Sequence Event Archive provides time-ordered evidence for later operational review.
S158: The North Protection Panel contains the protection equipment associated with feeder protection functions.
S159: The Control Room Operator uses indications from the North Protection Panel to assess feeder protection operations and related alarms.
S160: The Transformer Protection Panel is dedicated to protection functions associated with the power transformer rather than feeder protection.
S161: The Transformer Protection Panel provides local indication of transformer protection operation for assessment during an alarm response.
S162: The Control Room Operator considers the condition of the Station DC System when alarms or protection indications suggest a possible control-power concern.
S163: A breaker status discrepancy is treated as an abnormal condition until its cause and operational significance are understood.
S164: The Engineering Workstation is used for authorized review of protection and event information, not as a substitute for immediate operational assessment.
S165: The Protection Relay Engineer supports investigation when relay indications, settings concerns, or event evidence require technical interpretation.
S166: The Substation Field Crew confirms device identity and local conditions before carrying out an authorized operation.
S167: The Substation Supervisor is consulted when the alarm response requires escalation beyond routine operator actions.
S168: The Control Room Operator produces the Clearance Handoff Memo when an unresolved alarm condition requires a formal handoff.
S169: The Switching Desk Coordinator confirms operational handback before the associated state-change evidence is considered available for authorized engineering review.
S170: After handback, the Control Room Operator verifies that alarm status, equipment status, and recorded evidence are consistent before closing the response.
S171: The station communications design separates supervisory requests, bay-level execution, and protection action so loss of one layer does not silently substitute for another.
S172: Station Gateway brokers authorized station traffic across control-room and bay networks, applying configured protocol mappings, addressing, and access controls.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
